The middle و appears as the long ā of حَابَ and is retained in the lexical/root analysis even when the surface form is حُوب.
حَوْبٌ and حُوبٌ are lexical vocalic variants of the same noun, not separate rows.
Article, case ending and the Qur’anic accusative were not counted.

The current Qur’anic form plus four independently attested, morphologically useful same-root forms are established. The hollow middle radical is explained honestly; no shell, case, pronoun or bare-radical padding is used.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%B9. The entry attests رَاعَ, أَرَاعَ, رَيَّعَ, تَرَيَّعَ and the noun رَيْع with increase, growth and elevation branches.
The middle ي is represented by the hollow ā of رَاعَ and the yāʾ-bearing noun رَيْع; the Qur’anic رِيع is a lexical vocalic form, not a separate root.
رَيْعٌ is a close vocalic noun variant of the Qur’anic رِيع and was not counted separately from the current noun.

The evidence securely establishes the Qur’anic noun and its plural, but does not establish four additional learner-useful forms under the canonical س و ح analysis without importing the disputed س ي ح travelling branch or counting shell/near-duplicate noun variants. This is a reviewed limited family, not an unfinished blocked family.

Cairo Arabic Language Academy root entry: https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/%D8%B3%D9%88%D8%AD. The Academy’s ساحة entry defines the open space/courtyard and gives the plural ساحٌ and سُوحٌ; classical lexica likewise derive الساحة from the hollow root س و ح.
The middle و is preserved by the plural سُوح; the long ā in سَاحَة is the expected hollow-root surface outcome.
The verb سَاحَ meaning travelled/roamed was rejected because its root assignment is disputed with س ي ح and would require a documented normalization decision before being used here.
سَاحَةٌ is the lexical stem already present in بِسَاحَتِهِمْ; prefix, case and possessive removal do not count.
سَاحٌ and سُوحٌ are plural variants of the same noun; only سُوحٌ was retained.
سَاحَ: travelled / roamed
سَاحَةٌ: The current بِسَاحَتِهِمْ already contains this noun; removing بِـ, case and ـهِمْ would be shell normalization, not a new Ṣarf row.
سَاحٌ: A lexical plural variant of the same noun, but using both سَاحٌ and سُوحٌ would provide duplicate number teaching rather than a genuinely distinct morphological contrast.

The current Qur’anic form plus four independently attested, morphologically useful same-root forms are established. The hollow middle radical is explained honestly; no shell, case, pronoun or bare-radical padding is used.
